item.title: Nile Crocodile vs Black Mamba: The Deadly Encounter That Defies Size
item.description:
Made with Restream Studio. Livestream on 30+ platforms at once via https://restream.io
Nile Crocodile vs Black Mamba — what happens when one of Africa's most powerful reptiles takes on one of its most dangerous venomous snakes?
The Nile crocodile is an enormous apex predator capable of overpowering a wide range of prey. The black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis), meanwhile, is one of Africa's most medically significant venomous snakes, armed with a potent neurotoxic venom and capable of striking repeatedly when threatened.
So what happens when these two African predators collide?
This wildlife documentary examines the crocodile vs black mamba confrontation and the biology behind it. Rather than relying on internet myths about crocodile "immunity" to snake venom, we look at what has actually been documented and what researchers know about the two animals.
A real encounter between a Nile crocodile and a black mamba was filmed in Kruger National Park, South Africa, on the banks of the Shingwedzi River, providing a remarkable example of this rare predator confrontation.
The black mamba's venom is predominantly neurotoxic, and clinical symptoms following envenomation can develop rapidly. Its reputation comes from a combination of venom potency, speed, size and defensive behavior.
But here's the question: Why would a massive Nile crocodile risk attacking a highly venomous snake? Is the crocodile actually protected from the venom? Does size determine the outcome? Can a black mamba's bite seriously threaten a crocodile? And what does this confrontation reveal about African predator behavior, reptile biology and survival in the wild?
Watch until the end as we break down the encounter using documented wildlife observations and scientific information.

item.title: Apex Files Honey Badger Wars Part 3 — The Den
item.description:
Apex Files Honey Badger Wars — The Den - A black-backed jackal pack breaches a honey badger den while the mother is away foraging. What happens in the next ninety seconds changes how scientists understand honey badger den defense — and reveals a detail about den construction almost no wildlife footage captures correctly.
This is Part 3 of the Honey Badger Wars series. We break down why honey badger mothers rarely sleep in the same den two nights running, why a den's single narrow entrance is both its greatest weakness and its best defense, and what actually happens when that defense fails and a predator starts digging in from the side.
Real research grounds every claim in this video — from den-switching behavior to jackal pack-hunting limits to the survival data on mothers who relocate cubs immediately after a breach attempt.
Catch up on the series here: [https://youtu.be/V1y4MR49lN8] and [https://youtu.be/yhsRfb55kUE] — watch from the beginning for the full story building into this episode.
